after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}30x\,dV
$$

where $R$ is the type I region given by 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1-x,\,0\le z\le 1-x-y}.
$$
after.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}30x\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x-y}30x\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x-y}30x\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}[{\int }_{0}^{1-x-y}30x\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}[30xz]_{z=0}^{z=1-x-y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}30x(1-x-y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}30x-30{x}^{2}-30xy\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}30x-30{x}^{2}-30xy\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1-x}30x-30{x}^{2}-30xy\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[30xy-30{x}^{2}y-15x{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=1-x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}30x(1-x)-30{x}^{2}(1-x)-15x(1-x)^{2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{3}-30{x}^{2}+15x\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{3}-30{x}^{2}+15x\,dx & ={[\frac{15}{4}{x}^{4}-10{x}^{3}+\frac{15}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(\frac{15}{4}-10+\frac{15}{2})-0 \\  & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}30x\,dV
$$

where $R$ is the type I region given by 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1-x,\,0\le z\le 1-x-y}.
$$
content.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}30x\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x-y}30x\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x-y}30x\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}[{\int }_{0}^{1-x-y}30x\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}[30xz]_{z=0}^{z=1-x-y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}30x(1-x-y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}30x-30{x}^{2}-30xy\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}30x-30{x}^{2}-30xy\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1-x}30x-30{x}^{2}-30xy\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[30xy-30{x}^{2}y-15x{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=1-x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}30x(1-x)-30{x}^{2}(1-x)-15x(1-x)^{2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{3}-30{x}^{2}+15x\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{3}-30{x}^{2}+15x\,dx & ={[\frac{15}{4}{x}^{4}-10{x}^{3}+\frac{15}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(\frac{15}{4}-10+\frac{15}{2})-0 \\  & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 1+2y},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 2}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070095/assets/ac3eafe926b84588703bb8a56a1529ebe1352d25764a523b97c684a4f4e95201.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1+2y}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}x\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1+2y}x\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1+2y}x\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1+2y}x\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[xz]_{z=0}^{z=1+2y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}x(1+2y)\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$
